svg.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, 'Noto Sans', sans-serif
svg.title: CloudCart AWS EKS Architecture
svg.desc: Production-style AWS architecture showing Terraform provisioning, Docker and ECR image flow, EKS workloads (frontend, product-service, order-service, worker), AWS service integrations, security, networking and observability. Animated: request flow, async queue, events, identity and provisioning.
svg.metadata: CloudCart architecture diagram. Source of truth: the repository (terraform/, kubernetes/, helm/, application/, scripts/). AWS service icons: AWS Architecture Icons (Icon package 07312026), embedded as inline vector symbols; no external resources.
svg.text: Production-style AWS EKS platform · Terraform → Docker/ECR → EKS pods → AWS services
3 AZ · private nodes · isolated DB subnets
Pod Identity · no static AWS keys
Derived from the repository (Terraform · Kubernetes · Helm · Dockerfiles · app source). Dashed = optional / off by default.

g.text: local image store · trivy scan if installed
immutable · never :latest · ECR login via STS token
docker push over HTTPS · layers stored in S3-backed ECR
no AWS ID copied by hand · image tag must be immutable
With a domain: user → Route 53 → CloudFront → https origin.<domain> → ALB (WAF attached) → pod.
Without a domain (default): user → ALB DNS name over HTTP; Route 53 / ACM / CloudFront create nothing.
WAF is REGIONAL: it is attached to the ALB by the Ingress, not placed in front of CloudFront.
ACM issues the ALB cert (and a us-east-1 copy for CloudFront); DNS-validated in Route 53.
AWS-managed · highly available across AZs · no instances for you to run or patch
control-plane logs → CloudWatch: api · audit · authenticator (7 d retention)
rate limit 2000/5 min + AWS managed rule groups
built by AWS LB Controller from the Ingress · target-type ip · health /health · ACM TLS
HTTP→HTTPS redirect · access logs → S3 (29-alb) · attached WAF ACL
egress for private subnets · prod: 1 per AZ
serverless pod: own microVM, no EC2 node to manage
CloudCart services do not run on Fargate
1 of N · AZ a · b · c
Spot + On-Demand · c/m/r gen 5+ · large–2xlarge · AL2023 · encrypted gp3 · IMDSv2 · limit 16 vCPU
consolidation: WhenEmptyOrUnderutilized · app pods are untainted → may also land on the system node group
Pod Security: baseline enforce · restricted warn / audit | NetworkPolicy: default-deny ingress + allow rules
every pod: non-root · seccomp RuntimeDefault · startup/liveness/readiness probes · PDB minAvailable 1 · topologySpread (AZ + node) · rolling update maxUnavailable 0 · HPA on CPU
Spot warning → EventBridge → SQS → Karpenter drains node.
Cluster Autoscaler: optional, off by default (41).
DATABASE SUBNETS · AZ a·b·c · isolated (no default route)
VPC ENDPOINTS · private paths to AWS APIs (PrivateLink)
INTERFACE · ENI + private DNS · SG 443 from VPC CIDR · lab: 1 AZ
Private: 0.0.0.0/0 → NAT · S3 + DynamoDB prefix lists
Pods call AWS over private IPs: private DNS resolves sts / ssm / sqs / events / secretsmanager to endpoint ENIs; S3 and DynamoDB use gateway routes (no NAT cost).
Nodes pull images with the node IAM role via ecr.api + ecr.dkr; layers come from S3 through the gateway endpoint.
eks-secrets → envelope-encrypts Kubernetes Secrets in etcd
data → ECR · EBS · EFS · S3 · RDS · DynamoDB · Valkey · SQS · SNS · Backup vault
rds + redis credentials, KMS-encrypted · read at runtime via Pod Identity
no Kubernetes Secret objects, nothing secret in Git or YAML
/cloudcart/lab/* → endpoints, queue URL, bus, topic, bucket, table, secret ARNs
plain config only — values are not secrets; IAM scoped to the prefix
no static AWS keys in Pods
Secrets read at runtime, never baked in
encryption in transit: TLS to Valkey / RDS-ready
on-demand · PITR · KMS · product-service scan / get / put
reached privately via the DynamoDB gateway endpoint
SSE-KMS · versioning · public access blocked · presigned GET URLs (5 min)
product-service put / get via the S3 gateway endpoint
RDS PostgreSQL and ElastiCache Valkey sit in the isolated database subnets inside the VPC (left).
BLOCK · one node at a time (RWO)
SHARED FILESYSTEM · many pods / many AZs (RWX)
mount targets in private subnets · SG: NFS 2049 from nodes · EFS backup policy
OBJECT · accessed by SDK, not mounted
S3 images bucket (above) — product-service uses it via Pod Identity, no volume involved
Core CloudCart services are stateless; EBS / EFS are exercised by lab pods (ebs-demo, efs-demo).
SA name == Pod Identity association (namespace cloudcart) · agent serves credentials on 169.254.170.23 · credentials are short-lived
DynamoDB · S3 images + KMS · Secrets (redis) · SSM read
Secrets Manager (RDS) · SQS SendMessage · SSM read
SQS receive/delete · Secrets (RDS) · EventBridge PutEvents · SSM
Platform add-ons (Karpenter, LB Controller, ExternalDNS, CloudWatch agent, EBS/EFS CSI) use their own Pod Identity roles.
People / CI: IAM → STS → EKS access entries → Kubernetes RBAC · GitHub OIDC deploy role (optional, 46-cicd).
multi-region trail · log validation · → S3 (90 d)
EKS audit-log findings · runtime monitoring optional
Security groups: nodes · rds · redis · efs · vpce (SG → SG rules)
IMDSv2 required · hop limit 1 on all node templates
SG for Pods (branch ENI) · optional, needs pod_eni
Egress lock-down policy set · lab exercise
EKS add-on amazon-cloudwatch-observability (CloudWatch agent + Fluent Bit), Pod Identity role
EKS control plane: api · audit · authenticator
Container Insights: application · performance · dataplane · host
WAF logs · Lambda logs · ALB access logs → S3
Container Insights: pod & node CPU, memory, network, restarts
Spot / rebalance / health events → SQS → Karpenter
CloudTrail: every AWS API call (security panel)
exercise only — NOT deployed in Terraform
orders DLQ depth · oldest message age · Lambda errors · events DLQ · RDS CPU / free storage · DynamoDB throttles
SQS · Lambda · RDS · DynamoDB · Container Insights widgets
Telemetry from EKS control plane, nodes / pods and AWS services flows into one place (green dashed lines).
Security telemetry (CloudTrail · GuardDuty · Config · Security Hub) sits in the security panel above.
3 AZ subnets · nodes & pods spread by topologySpread
ReplicaSets · HPA · PDB minAvailable 1 · Karpenter replaces nodes
SQS decouples order-service from worker · retry + DLQ (kept 14 d)
automated backups · 7-day PITR (Single-AZ in lab; multi_az optional)
EBS VolumeSnapshot · EFS backup policy · S3 versioning
daily 05:00 UTC · 7 d · RDS + DynamoDB + EFS · cross-region copy optional
EventBridge archive (3 d) + events DLQ · Spot warnings drained
roll back by tag · ECR keeps last 30 · scan on push
single NAT in lab → 1 per AZ in prod · VPC endpoints reduce NAT dependency
terraform apply per folder · state versioned in S3
Terraform builds AWS in dependency order (bottom strip).
Immutable tags are pushed to Amazon ECR.
Helm applies workloads; EKS schedules pods onto compute.
Edge → WAF → ALB → pod IPs (blue request flow ①–⑦).
Pods use IAM-based identity to reach data & messaging.
Logs, metrics, API activity and findings feed CloudWatch & security services.
AWS service icons: official AWS Architecture Icons (embedded). Terraform, Karpenter
and pod marks are neutral vector drawings, not official logos.
Container Insights · node & pod metrics, logs
terraform apply → AWS APIs create every resource above

49 independent root modules · one state object each · apply order = folder number (16-kms is applied right after 03) · each reads earlier outputs via terraform_remote_state · scripts/tf.sh: deps → fmt → validate → plan → apply → verify
terraform_remote_state · later folders read earlier outputs (VPC → EKS → add-ons → data → edge). 99-capstone reads every layer and publishes the Helm values; it creates no AWS resources.
Shared snippets terraform/_common and _common_k8s (providers, backend, k8s auth) are copied into each folder by scripts/sync-common.sh — they are not state units.
Remote state backend (created by 00-bootstrap on local state)
s3://cloudcart-tfstate-<account>-<region>/<environment>/<folder>/terraform.tfstate · versioned · SSE-S3 · public access blocked · TLS-only · native S3 lockfile
Terraform owns anything with an AWS lifecycle or IAM blast radius · Helm / kubectl own app workloads
